title: Increased Pseudorandomness Threshold
summary: For the stated local permutation model, logarithmic-wise independence is sufficient for pseudorandomness; the conjecture asks whether 4-wise independence suffices after doubling the composition rounds.

formal_statement.body: Let $P$ be a randomized permutation $P:\{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}^n$ such that each output bit depends on only a constant number of input bits. The unresolved question is whether, if the $T$-fold composition $P^T$ is negligibly far from $4$-wise independence, then increasing the number of composition rounds to $2T$ makes the result pseudorandom; specifically, whether there exists a polynomial $p$ such that $P^{2T}$ is a pseudorandom permutation under these conditions.

scope.domain: Cryptographic pseudorandomness and limited independence of randomized permutations with constant local dependence.
assumptions: P is a randomized permutation from {0,1}^n to {0,1}^n.
Each output bit of P depends on only a constant number of input bits.
The T-fold composition of P is negligibly far from 4-wise independence.
parameters: n: bit length of the permutation domain and range
T: baseline number of composition rounds
2T: doubled number of composition rounds in the target
p: polynomial whose existence is asserted in the target
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the stated 4-wise-independence condition guarantees that doubling the composition rounds yields a pseudorandom permutation for some polynomial p.

citations.label: When Simple Permutations Mix Poorly: Limited Independence Does Not Imply Pseudorandomness

progress.summary: The source states this as Conjecture 4, titled "Increased Pseudorandomness Threshold." It presents the unresolved implication from the T-fold composition being negligibly far from 4-wise independence to the doubled composition being a pseudorandom permutation.
citation_labels: Jesko Dujmovic et al., When Simple Permutations Mix Poorly: Limited Independence Does Not Imply Pseudorandomness
